patch.summary:
Choose Brandwatch only if your buying job matches “Enterprise consumer intelligence and social listening suite — demo/custom packaging (no pu” rather than WhatConverts's shape. Choose WhatConverts only if your buying job matches “Lead tracking and call attribution for marketers and agencies — Call Tracking from $30/mo ” rather than Brandwatch's shape. Workflow advantage: Brandwatch leans brand-monitoring; WhatConverts leans lead-generation. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Positioning: Brandwatch is Enterprise consumer intelligence and social listening suite — demo/custom packaging (no public list prices).; WhatConverts is Lead tracking and call attribution for marketers and agencies — Call Tracking from $30/mo with Plus/Pro/Elite ladders..
- Company-size focus: Brandwatch (mid-market, enterprise) vs WhatConverts (micro, small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: Brandwatch-leaning brand-monitoring vs WhatConverts-leaning lead-generation.
- Researched limits: Brandwatch — No public list-price transparency; WhatConverts — Specialist lead/call tracking — not a full marketing suite.

Limitations — Brandwatch: No public list-price transparency; Enterprise sales cycle and packaging complexity; WhatConverts: Specialist lead/call tracking — not a full marketing suite; Usage overages can dominate TCO.
